evidence: junk_imagery: hook@0.3 to seg1:end: every unit tile is the same generic purple starfield-over-hills clip art. It says nothing about temperature, and a pile of 'night sky' tiles cannot show 293 K against 2.7 K.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: A flat teal square fills the frame with a meaningless '29400T' for the whole segment. 'NASA's Cold Atom Lab (ISS)' appears as a tiny label at its edge, and Data hovers on top in an unchanging pose. The narration's 5,000 light-years vs 250 miles is never shown.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The distance comparison went to a generic area-square renderer with the unit converted into an unreadable huge number ('29400T'). The ISS value is too small to draw, so there is no picture of the comparison at all.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Show the distance contrast physically: Data on a launch pad or ladder reaches the ISS freezer at 250 miles while the Boomerang Nebula drops away on a log-scale road or tape that runs off into deep space. Use readable units ('250 miles' vs '5,000 light-years') and keep every label inside the frame.
